intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots inside a protected marine sanctuary. Families can swim alongside colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in calm, shallow waters. Reservations are required in advance and an educational video is mandatory before entry.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A memorable evening blending food, music, and storytelling.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Walk through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations and native Hawaiian plant exhibits.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's incredible marine life at one of the top aquariums in the Pacific. Walk through a 54-foot underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and hundreds of tropical fish. Interactive exhibits and touch pools make it a perfect educational outing for families with children of all ages.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Day with Cliff Diving at Black Rock
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing beach day at one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Older kids and adults can watch or participate in the famous cliff diving tradition at Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock), while younger children enjoy the calm, clear waters perfect for swimming and building sandcastles.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Day with Cliff Diving at Black Rock
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing beach day at one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Older kids and adults can watch or participate in the famous cliff diving tradition at Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock), while younger children enjoy the calm, clear waters perfect for swimming and building sandcastles.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Flight arrives midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, collect luggage and take the affordable TheBus Route 23 from the airport toward East Oahu (approx $3/person). Check in to the Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a short walk to nearby Maunalua Bay Beach Park to dip your toes in the ocean and decompress from travel. The calm waters are perfect for kids.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to nearby Koko Marina Center for a casual family dinner. Visit Zippy's Restaurant, a beloved local chain offering affordable Hawaiian plate lunches and comfort food. Budget roughly $10-15 per adult, $6-8 per child.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the Honolulu Airport food court (Panda Express, Subway, or local options around $10-12).
meals.dinner: Zippy's at Koko Marina Center - Hawaiian plate lunches, saimin noodles, and chili rice. Budget-friendly local favorite.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a TheBus monthly pass or stored-value card (HOLO Card) at the airport or a nearby 7-Eleven to save on transportation throughout the trip. Stop at a grocery store like Times Supermarket or Foodland near Koko Marina to stock up on breakfast items, snacks, and drinks to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve snorkeling adventure (opens at 6:45 AM, arrive early to secure entry - reservations required online). Entry fee is $25/adult, children 12 and under are FREE. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible to avoid rental fees, or rent on-site for $12. The bay is teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish - a magical family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay closes to the public (it closes at 1:30 PM on Mondays), head to nearby Koko Head Crater Trail for a moderate hike up 1,048 steps made from old railway ties. Kids 8+ typically manage this well. Stunning panoramic views of East Oahu await at the top. Free to hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rinse off and relax. Head to Koko Marina for shave ice at Island Snow Hawaii (made famous by President Obama). Budget $5-8 per serving. Pick up groceries for tomorrow's breakfast.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased yesterday - cereal, fruit, yogurt, and juice.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the hotel to enjoy at Hanauma Bay's picnic area. Save $15-20 per person vs. buying food there.
meals.dinner: Poke bowl from Tamura's Fine Wine & Liquors at Aina Haina (a short bus ride) - fresh, affordable poke bowls starting at $12. A true Hawaiian experience.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked online in advance at hawaiistateparks.reserveamerica.com. Slots fill weeks ahead, especially in summer. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only - chemical sunscreens are banned at the bay. Bring water shoes as the reef entry can be rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take TheBus to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (free, parking $5 or take the bus). This paved 2-mile round-trip trail is stroller-friendly and offers dramatic cliffs, whale watching (seasonal), and stunning views of the Windward Coast and offshore islands. One of Oahu's most scenic and budget-friendly hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Waimanalo Beach, consistently rated one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches. The long stretch of powdery white sand and calm turquoise waters is ideal for families. Free entry. Build sandcastles, swim, and enjoy the backdrop of the Ko'olau Mountains. Bring your own snacks and drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the Waimanalo Poi Company or local roadside stands for fresh Hawaiian produce. Return to East Oahu and cook a simple dinner using groceries. Alternatively, visit Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kaimuki for authentic Hawaiian cuisine like kalua pig and laulau at very reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast - scrambled eggs, toast, and fruit prepared in the room.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Waimanalo Beach - sandwiches, chips, fruit, and cold drinks from the cooler.
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods (Kaimuki) - traditional Hawaiian plate lunches featuring kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert. Meals from $14-18.

day_by_day.notes: Waimanalo Beach has limited facilities so bring your own supplies. The area is beloved by locals and tends to be less crowded than tourist beaches on the South Shore. Keep an eye out for Hawaiian monk seals resting on the beach - maintain a 50-foot distance as required by law.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus into downtown Honolulu to visit Iolani Palace, the only royal palace in the United States ($25/adult, $5/child 5-12, under 5 free). The self-guided audio tour is engaging for older kids and teaches Hawaiian history. Afterward, walk to the nearby King Kamehameha Statue for a photo opportunity (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Chinatown for an affordable cultural experience. Browse the historic Oahu Market, Maunakea Marketplace, and colorful lei shops. Grab lunch from one of the many cheap and delicious restaurants. Then walk to the waterfront Aloha Tower Marketplace (free to explore) for views of Honolulu Harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset at Ala Moana Beach Park (free), one of Honolulu's best urban beaches. The calm lagoon is safe for children. Then walk through Ala Moana Center (Hawaii's largest mall) for free air-conditioning and window shopping before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast - overnight oats or cereal with banana.
meals.lunch: Chinatown dim sum or noodle soup at Little Village Noodle House or Legend Seafood Restaurant. Budget $8-12 per person.
meals.dinner: Marukai Pacific Market food court near Ala Moana or grab affordable Japanese bento boxes from ABC Stores. Budget $10-15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: TheBus fare is $3/adult and $1.50/children. Purchase a HOLO Card for convenience. Iolani Palace is closed on Sundays and Mondays, so Wednesday is perfect. Chinatown can be lively but stay on the main tourist streets with kids. Bring a light jacket for the bus rides as the AC can be cold.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument, Oahu's most iconic landmark (entry $5/person or $10/car). The 1.6-mile round-trip hike to the summit crater rim takes about 1.5 hours and rewards you with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Bring plenty of water as it can be hot. Best done early to avoid midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bus to Waikiki Beach for the classic Hawaii beach experience. Enjoy the free beach, people-watch, and let the kids play in the surf. Try a free outrigger canoe push from one of the beach boys (tips appreciated). Walk the Kalakaua Avenue strip and browse the International Market Place.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show at Kuhio Beach Park in Waikiki (Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday evenings at 6:30 PM - free!). Watch traditional hula dancing and torch lighting ceremony. A magical, authentic, and completely free cultural experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast - yogurt parfait with granola and fresh pineapple.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In in Kapahulu (near Waikiki) - an iconic local plate lunch spot. Beef stew plate or loco moco for $10-13. A must-try local institution.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries from Foodland or grab affordable plate lunches from one of the many takeout spots near Waikiki. Eat at Kapiolani Park picnic tables to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head tickets should be reserved online in advance at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Arrive at opening (6 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Waikiki Beach is free but beach chair and umbrella rentals cost $30+/day - bring your own beach towels and umbrella from the hotel. The hula show at Kuhio Beach is a highlight - arrive 15 minutes early for good seating.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the North Shore via TheBus (Route 52 Wahiawa/Circle Island - about 1.5-2 hours, $3/person). Visit Haleiwa Town, the charming surf town with colorful shops, galleries, and the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice ($4-6 per serving). Walk the historic town and enjoy the laid-back vibe. Haleiwa Beach Park is great for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (home of the famous Banzai Pipeline). In August, the summer swells are gentle and the water is calm and safe for swimming. Watch local surfers and bodyboarders. All beaches are free. Walk along the scenic 2-mile Sunset Beach stretch.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku on the way back - a North Shore institution. Garlic shrimp plates are $15 and absolutely delicious. Eat at the picnic tables under the trees. Return to East Oahu via TheBus in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before catching the bus - pack extra snacks for the journey.
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice for a treat, plus pick up fresh fruit from a North Shore farm stand (mangoes, papayas, and coconuts sold cheaply roadside). Pack sandwiches from the hotel.
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Famous Shrimp Truck in Kahuku - scampi or hot and spicy garlic shrimp plate with rice and salad for $15. Worth every penny.

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore bus journey is long but scenic and very affordable. Alternatively, rent a car for the day through Turo or a budget rental agency for $40-60 to give more flexibility. In August, North Shore waves are small and calm (big wave season is November-February), making it perfect for family swimming. Bring sunscreen, hats, and lots of water for the beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum, Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum ($24.95/adult, $16.95/child 4-17, under 4 free). The Hawaiian Hall is a stunning three-story Victorian building showcasing Hawaiian artifacts, royal regalia, and natural history exhibits. Plan for 2-3 hours. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Pali Lookout (Nu'uanu Pali State Wayside) for dramatic views of the Windward Coast from 1,200 feet elevation. The lookout is free (parking $7 or take the bus). The wind is famously intense - hold onto hats and small children! Learn about the historic 1795 Battle of Nu'uanu. Combine with a short walk in the lush Ko'olau rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaimuki neighborhood for dinner on Waialae Avenue, known as one of Honolulu's best dining streets. Visit Kaimuki Superette for creative but affordable sandwiches and local comfort food. Browse the Saturday farmers market at KCC (Kapiolani Community College) if timing works (7:30 AM-11 AM).

meals.breakfast: KCC Farmers Market (7:30-11 AM) - sample fresh local produce, malasadas, acai bowls, and tropical fruits. Budget $10-15 for a delicious market breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and eat at Pali Lookout picnic area, or grab a quick bite near the Bishop Museum.
meals.dinner: Kaimuki Superette - creative sandwiches and local comfort food for $12-16. Or try Genki Sushi in Kaimuki for affordable conveyor belt sushi at $1.50-3.50 per plate.

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is one of the best value educational experiences in Hawaii, especially for families. Check for free family days or discounts through the hotel concierge or AAA. The KCC Farmers Market is a Saturday morning institution - go early for the best selection. Pali Lookout can be very windy and cool, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning drive or bus to Lanikai Beach in Kailua, consistently ranked among the world's top beaches. The calm, crystal-clear turquoise water and powdery white sand are breathtaking. Free to access (walk through public beach access paths between homes). Swim, snorkel, and enjoy views of the Mokulua Islands. Arrive early as parking is limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bike the Lanikai Pillbox Hike (free) - a 1.8-mile round trip trail to WWII-era military bunkers with stunning views of Kailua Bay and the Mokulua Islands. Moderate difficulty but doable for most families with older kids. Then explore Kailua Town for shopping at local boutiques and the famous Kalapawai Market.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset at Kailua Beach Park, one of Oahu's most beautiful beaches. Then grab dinner in Kailua Town before heading back to East Oahu. Kailua has excellent dining options at various price points.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast - pack fruit and granola bars for the beach morning.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua - gourmet sandwiches, salads, and local specialties in a charming deli setting. Budget $12-15 per person.
meals.dinner: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua for Hawaiian-style comfort food, or Whole Foods Market Kailua for affordable hot bar and prepared foods ($10-15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has no facilities (no restrooms, no parking lot), so use the restrooms at Kailua Beach Park first and bring everything you need. The Pillbox Hike is best done in the morning before it gets too hot. The trail can be steep and exposed so bring plenty of water and wear proper shoes. Kailua is a wonderful, less touristy alternative to Waikiki for beach days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii in Waimanalo ($39.99/adult, $29.99/child 3-12, under 3 free). This family-friendly marine park features dolphin shows, penguin encounters, sea turtle exhibits, and a Hawaiian reef aquarium. Look for online discount codes or Groupon deals that can reduce admission by 20-30%. Plan for a full morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Sea Life Park, head to nearby Sandy Beach Park, famous for its powerful shore break and bodysurfing. Note: the surf at Sandy Beach can be dangerous for inexperienced swimmers - supervise children carefully and stay in the designated swimming areas. The beach itself is beautiful and great for watching skilled bodysurfers. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Final East Oahu evening - visit Koko Head District Park for sunset views of Koko Crater and the surrounding landscape. Pick up dinner from a local plate lunch spot and enjoy a picnic. Alternatively, splurge slightly at Roy's Restaurant in Hawaii Kai for a special family dinner (happy hour specials available).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast - make it hearty before the full day out. Scrambled eggs, toast, fruit, and juice.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Sea Life Park or bring packed lunches to save money (check if outside food is permitted).
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina Center - craft beers for adults and great food for the family. Pizzas and burgers from $15-20. Happy hour deals available.

day_by_day.notes: Check Sea Life Park's website for current shows and feeding schedules to plan your visit efficiently. Look for Groupon or discount codes before purchasing tickets - savings can be significant. Sandy Beach has a strong reputation for injuries due to its powerful shore break - swim with extreme caution and never turn your back on the waves. Lifeguards are on duty but the beach is known as one of Hawaii's most dangerous.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning - wake up early for one last sunrise snorkel at Hanauma Bay (if you have a reservation) or a peaceful walk along the East Oahu coastline. Visit the Halona Blowhole Lookout (free) along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway for dramatic ocean views and the famous Halona Beach Cove (the secluded beach from the movie From Here to Eternity). Watch for spinner dolphins offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, check out, and pack up. Spend your final hours at Koko Marina Center for last-minute souvenir shopping. Budget-friendly souvenir tips: ABC Stores for macadamia nuts and local treats, Longs Drugs for affordable Hawaiian coffee and chocolates, and local farmers markets for handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Honolulu Airport via TheBus or arrange a shuttle. Allow 2.5-3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Enjoy your final Hawaiian meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before departure.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast - treat the family to malasadas from Leonard's Bakery (if passing through Honolulu) or make a special hotel breakfast with remaining groceries.
meals.lunch: Poke bowl from a local shop near Koko Marina or a plate lunch to-go - your last taste of authentic Hawaiian food.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the airport. Honolulu Airport has improved dining options including local Hawaiian food options.

day_by_day.notes: Return any rental equipment, beach gear, or library books. Double-check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Agricultural inspection is required when leaving Hawaii - dispose of any fresh fruits, vegetables, or plants before going through security. Take one last look at the Pacific Ocean and soak in the aloha spirit before heading home. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and collecting luggage, check in to the Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get oriented and enjoy the ocean views. Pick up groceries or snacks at a nearby store for the room.
day_by_day.evening: Casual welcome dinner at a nearby local spot in East Oahu. Explore the neighborhood and enjoy a relaxed first evening watching the sunset from the beach near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Honolulu International Airport or a fast-casual spot near the hotel like Kono's or a local plate lunch truck.
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — a beloved mid-range Hawaiian fusion restaurant just minutes from Hanauma Bay, perfect for a celebratory first night dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — prioritize settling in, hydrating, and getting a good night's sleep to enjoy the rest of the trip. Pre-book your Hanauma Bay snorkeling reservation online tonight if not already done, as spots fill up fast.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve first thing in the morning (arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat the crowds and heat). Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in this protected marine sanctuary. Gear rentals available on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive to Sandy Beach Park (just 5 minutes away) for a relaxing afternoon on one of Oahu's most scenic stretches of shore. Older kids can watch experienced bodyboarders tackle the waves — swimming here can be rough, so stick to wading and beach play.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a walk along the Makapuu coastline lookout area if energy allows, then head back for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or pack snacks from the grocery store — Hanauma Bay fills up fast so an early start is essential.
meals.lunch: Shrimp trucks along Kalanianaole Highway or a plate lunch from a local deli near Sandy Beach.
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Hawaii Kai — family-friendly, mid-range, great pizzas, burgers, and local craft beers with a waterfront view.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges a small entry fee per person. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned in the preserve. Bring water shoes for the rocky entry into the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Waimea Valley on the North Shore of Oahu (approximately 45–55 minutes from East Oahu). Begin the Waimea Valley Hike through a stunning botanical garden filled with tropical plants and historical Hawaiian cultural sites. The paved, family-friendly trail leads 0.75 miles to the beautiful 45-foot Waimea Falls waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in the freshwater pool beneath Waimea Falls (life jackets provided). After the hike, drive a few minutes to Waimea Bay Beach Park and relax on one of Oahu's most iconic beaches. In summer, the waters are calm and ideal for swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the laid-back surf town of Haleiwa on the North Shore — browse local shops, galleries, and grab famous shave ice before heading back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua on the way — famous for their guava pancakes and local breakfast plates.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from Waimea Valley's café or grab a plate from a food truck near Haleiwa town.
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (a North Shore institution) for garlic shrimp plates, then a sweet stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa before the drive home.

day_by_day.notes: Start early to avoid North Shore traffic and midday heat on the hike. Bring water, sunscreen, and comfortable closed-toe shoes for the valley trail. The drive back to East Oahu takes about an hour — plan to return before dark.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — drive about 20 minutes west from the hotel to hike the iconic Diamond Head crater trail. The 1.6-mile round-trip hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean. Moderate difficulty with some stairs — great for families with older kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a classic Hawaii afternoon. Rent surfboards or take a beginner surf lesson from one of the many beachside instructors. Stroll the famous Kalakaua Avenue, visit the Duke Kahanamoku statue, and let the kids splash in the gentle Waikiki surf.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Waikiki for the evening and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Watch the free hula and music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (held most evenings at sunset — check local schedule).

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Café near Diamond Head — a beloved local breakfast spot with açaí bowls, smoothies, and egg plates.
meals.lunch: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — incredibly popular, affordable, and delicious Japanese udon with a local twist. Expect a short line but it moves fast.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic oceanfront restaurant serving Hawaiian-inspired seafood and classics with a lively atmosphere. Mid-range pricing, great for families.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance timed entry reservations — book online before the trip. Arrive at the trailhead by 7:00–8:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Bring plenty of water for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie on the North Shore (about 35 minutes from East Oahu). Spend the morning exploring the six Polynesian island villages — Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Tahiti, Fiji, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like spear throwing, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center's afternoon shows and canoe pageant on the lagoon — a colorful, entertaining performance showcasing traditional Pacific island cultures. Great for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at the Polynesian Cultural Center for their evening luau dinner and the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' night show — a world-class fire knife dancing and cultural performance. This is one of Oahu's top family evening experiences.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery en route.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with many ticket packages, featuring Hawaiian and Pacific island cuisine.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian luau foods including kalua pork, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia coconut pudding.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets in advance online — combo packages including the luau and evening show offer the best value. Plan for a full day here; the center opens at noon but the luau and show run into the evening. This is a fantastic family day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Maui — fly or take a ferry inter-island (book in advance). Fly from Honolulu to Kahului Airport on Maui (approximately 30-minute flight on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest). Head straight to the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Maalaea. Walk through the stunning 54-foot underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and hundreds of tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kaanapali Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on this world-famous beach. Walk the Kaanapali Beachfront Boardwalk and explore the shops and resorts along the strip.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at Kaanapali Beach — a traditional Hawaiian ritual performed at sunset by a torch-lighting diver. Magical for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near the hotel before heading to the airport, or grab something at Honolulu Airport.
meals.lunch: Maui Ocean Center has a café, or grab a quick plate lunch in Maalaea before heading to Kaanapali.
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Kaanapali — a beloved mid-range beachfront restaurant on Kaanapali Beach with fresh fish, burgers, and live Hawaiian music. Perfect for the family after the cliff diving show.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance for the best mid-range fares. Consider staying overnight in Maui (Days 6–7) to reduce travel fatigue and enjoy more of the island — check if your hotel allows a 1-night pause or book a simple mid-range hotel in Kaanapali for one night.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight in Maui: Start the morning with a visit to the Road to Hana — drive the first scenic section of this legendary coastal highway, stopping at Twin Falls (an easy 20-minute walk to beautiful waterfalls) and the Garden of Eden Arboretum for lush jungle views and ocean overlooks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Road to Hana to Wai'anapanapa State Park — a dramatic black sand beach formed by lava. Explore sea caves, lava arches, and the striking contrast of black sand against turquoise water. Reserve a parking permit in advance online.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kahului and catch an evening inter-island flight back to Honolulu. Return to the Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay for a restful night.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from a local Maui bakery or hotel breakfast before hitting the Road to Hana.
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh banana bread, coconut candy, and local fruit from the famous farm stands (cash recommended).
meals.dinner: Grab a casual plate lunch or poke bowl near Kahului Airport before your flight, or eat at a casual spot in East Oahu upon return.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day experience on its own — this itinerary covers only the first scenic section to keep it manageable with a return flight in mind. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance parking reservations — book at hawaiistateparks.reserveamerica.com.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Maui day trip. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, and relax by the ocean near Hanauma Bay. Optional: gentle snorkel or beach walk along the nearby coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, ancient Polynesian navigation, volcanic geology, and natural history. Excellent for families and very manageable for kids.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chinatown in downtown Honolulu — a vibrant, walkable neighborhood with art galleries, local boutiques, and some of Honolulu's best restaurants. Stroll the historic streets and enjoy the multicultural atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel or nearby café — try Kaimana Farm Café near Hanauma Bay for fresh, local ingredients.
meals.lunch: Café at the Bishop Museum or a quick stop at a nearby deli.
meals.dinner: The Pig and the Lady in Chinatown — a beloved Honolulu restaurant with creative Vietnamese-inspired dishes and a lively atmosphere. Mid-range and family-welcoming.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately slower day to recharge after the Maui trip. The Bishop Museum is a great rainy-day backup option if weather turns — it's fully indoors and very engaging for all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Luau Dinner Experience prep day — start the morning with a visit to the USS Arizona Memorial at Pearl Harbor (about 35 minutes from East Oahu). Tour the historic site, visit the museum, and take the boat to the memorial above the sunken battleship. A powerful and educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a beautiful, calm, family-friendly beach adjacent to the world-famous Ala Moana Center. Swim, build sandcastles, and let the kids play in the gentle surf. Explore the Ala Moana Shopping Center for souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Old Lahaina Luau experience (if a Maui-based luau, coordinate travel) — OR enjoy a comparable Oahu luau such as the Paradise Cove Luau on the west shore of Oahu (about 45 minutes from East Oahu). Experience authentic hula dancing, fire knife performances, traditional Hawaiian foods, and cultural storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before Pearl Harbor — Island Brew Coffeehouse near Pearl Harbor is a great local option.
meals.lunch: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana Center — a beautiful mid-range restaurant with popovers and Pacific Rim cuisine, or grab casual food court bites at Ala Moana.
meals.dinner: Luau dinner included with the Paradise Cove Luau package — traditional kalua pig, poi, lomi lomi salmon, haupia, and more served buffet-style.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry tickets must be booked in advance at recreation.gov — they sell out weeks ahead. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but requires a timed pass. Arrive 30 minutes early. Book the luau well in advance as summer evenings fill up fast.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — take one last sunrise walk or snorkel at Hanauma Bay (early entry, no crowds). Soak in the beauty of the marine sanctuary one final time. Return to the hotel for a relaxed breakfast and begin packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay. Drive along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway one last time, stopping at the Makapuu Lighthouse Trail for a short, breezy coastal walk with sweeping views of the windward coast and offshore islands (Rabbit Island and Manana Island visible). Pick up last-minute souvenirs at a local shop.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Honolulu International Airport for departure. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and a final Hawaiian meal at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try açaí bowls, fresh papaya, and Kona coffee for a true island send-off.
meals.lunch: A farewell poke bowl lunch at Foodland Farms (a beloved local grocery chain with incredible poke counters) near East Oahu before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Honolulu International — try Makai Market Food Court or Island Brew Coffeehouse for a final taste of Hawaii before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: The Makapuu Lighthouse Trail is a 2-mile round trip with minimal elevation — easy and scenic, perfect for a final morning outing. If departing on an early flight, skip the lighthouse and go straight to the airport after breakfast. Don't forget to declare any fresh fruit or plant products — agricultural inspection is strict when leaving Hawaii.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots inside a protected marine sanctuary. Families can swim alongside colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in calm, shallow waters. Reservations are required in advance and an educational video is mandatory before entry.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A memorable evening blending food, music, and storytelling.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Walk through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations and native Hawaiian plant exhibits.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's incredible marine life at one of the top aquariums in the Pacific. Walk through a 54-foot underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and hundreds of tropical fish. Interactive exhibits and touch pools make it a perfect educational outing for families with children of all ages.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Day with Cliff Diving at Black Rock
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing beach day at one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Older kids and adults can watch or participate in the famous cliff diving tradition at Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock), while younger children enjoy the calm, clear waters perfect for swimming and building sandcastles.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight arrives midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay. Check in, unpack, and settle into your luxury accommodations. Take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get your first taste of East Oahu's stunning coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a premium oceanfront restaurant in East Oahu. Enjoy fresh Hawaiian seafood and local specialties while watching the sunset over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light bites at the airport or en route — recommend a stop at a local poke bowl spot near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — a celebrated fine-dining institution known for Hawaiian fusion cuisine, fresh fish, and breathtaking bay views, just minutes from Hanauma Bay

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00. Allow approximately 45–60 minutes for baggage claim and private transfer. Pre-arrange a luxury SUV or private car service. Request early check-in with the boutique hotel in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots right at your doorstep. Arrive early (reserve timed entry in advance) to enjoy the protected marine sanctuary before crowds build. Spot sea turtles, tropical fish, and vibrant coral reefs. Snorkel gear rental or bring premium personal gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a poolside lunch and relaxation. Spend the early afternoon exploring the scenic Koko Head Crater Trail or simply lounging on the private beach area near the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your hotel terrace or balcony, followed by a private in-room dining experience or a short drive to a top East Oahu restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — fresh tropical fruit, eggs Benedict, Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled fish tacos, açaí bowls, fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company Pub & Brewery (Hawaii Kai) or The Shack in Hawaii Kai for relaxed premium dining with local craft beers and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance timed-entry reservations — book online at least 2–3 days ahead. The bay opens at 6:45 AM; aim for the first entry slot for the best experience. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. This is a family highlight not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Waimea Valley on the North Shore of Oahu (approximately 1 hour from East Oahu). Begin the Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim — walk through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly trail featuring exotic tropical plants and wildlife, leading to the stunning 45-foot Waihi Falls waterfall. Swim in the natural pool beneath the falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the North Shore's famous beaches — visit Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay Beach for a relaxed afternoon on the sand. Older kids can bodysurf gentle summer waves while adults soak in the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to East Oahu via the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Enjoy a premium dinner in Kailua or Honolulu on the way back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoothie bowls, fresh pastries, tropical fruit platters
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (North Shore) — a legendary local experience; garlic shrimp plates eaten at picnic tables under banyan trees
meals.dinner: Mud Hen Water (Kaimuki, Honolulu) — an acclaimed farm-to-table Hawaiian restaurant with creative local dishes and an excellent cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley charges a modest admission fee. Life jackets are available at the waterfall swimming area for younger children. Wear water shoes for the trail and waterfall swim. The North Shore in August has calmer waters compared to winter — ideal for families. Start early to beat the midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — a short drive from East Oahu. Hike the iconic volcanic crater trail (moderate, ~1.6 miles round trip) for panoramic views of Honolulu and Waikiki. Arrive early to avoid heat and crowds. Book timed entry reservations in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a premium beach afternoon. Arrange a private surfing lesson through a luxury concierge surf school — instructors cater to all ages and skill levels. Younger children can try tandem surfing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the heart of Waikiki. Visit the luxury shops at Royal Hawaiian Center, then enjoy a world-class dinner at one of Honolulu's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a stop at Kaimana Beach Hotel's Hau Tree Restaurant for a scenic oceanfront breakfast
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the iconic Moana Surfrider hotel — enjoy sandwiches, salads, and tropical drinks on the historic Banyan Veranda
meals.dinner: Alan Wong's Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants, renowned for its innovative Hawaiian Regional Cuisine using locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head timed reservations are required and sell out quickly — book online 3–5 days in advance. The hike takes approximately 1.5 hours round trip. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Private surf lessons in Waikiki should be arranged through the hotel concierge for a premium, personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day inter-island excursion to Maui — take an early morning inter-island flight (approximately 25–35 minutes). Arrive on Maui and head directly to the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Maalaea. Discover Hawaii's incredible marine life, walk through a breathtaking underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks and rays, and enjoy interactive exhibits perfect for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kaanapali Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Spend a relaxing afternoon on the beach. Older kids and adventurous adults can witness or participate in the famous cliff diving at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), a beloved Kaanapali tradition. Snorkeling around Black Rock offers excellent visibility and abundant marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Old Lahaina Luau — an immersive, authentic Hawaiian cultural experience featuring traditional hula dancing, live music, storytelling, and a spectacular feast of traditional Hawaiian dishes including kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia. One of the finest luau experiences in all of Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure or at the Maui airport
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach (Kaanapali) — fresh fish, tropical cocktails, and stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Included in the Old Lahaina Luau experience — a full traditional Hawaiian feast

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance (Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines). Old Lahaina Luau reservations are essential — this iconic experience books up months ahead, especially in summer. Arrange a private car or rental on Maui for flexibility. Return flight to Oahu should be scheduled after the luau concludes (typically around 9:00–9:30 PM). This is a full and memorable day — the family highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the big Maui day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel. Late morning: arrange a private catamaran or sailing charter departing from nearby Koko Marina. Sail along the East Oahu coastline with snorkeling stops, whale watching (seasonal), and stunning views of the Ko'olau Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the sailing charter and enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the hotel pool or private beach area. Optional: book a luxury couples or family spa treatment at a nearby spa for rest and rejuvenation.
day_by_day.evening: Casual but upscale dinner in the Hawaii Kai neighborhood, followed by a family stargazing session on the hotel terrace or beach.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — eggs any style, acai bowls, fresh-baked pastries, Kona coffee and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Catered lunch on the catamaran — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruits, snacks, and beverages included in premium charter package
meals.dinner: Hy's Steak House (Waikiki/Honolulu) or Vintage Cave Honolulu for an extraordinary fine-dining experience — reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charters can be arranged through Hawaii Ocean Project or similar luxury providers. A half-day charter typically runs 4–5 hours. This is a wonderful day for families to bond on the water. Spa treatments at the hotel should be booked in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center on Oahu's North Shore (approximately 45 minutes from East Oahu). Explore six authentic Polynesian village experiences representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy live cultural demonstrations, canoe rides, and interactive activities — a world-class family attraction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch the spectacular IMAX film 'Hā: Breath of Life' and participate in hands-on cultural workshops including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a premium luau experience with reserved seating, a full buffet of Pacific Island foods, and a breathtaking evening show featuring over 100 performers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in premium admission packages; enjoy a variety of Pacific Island-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a comprehensive feast included with the evening show package

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the premium 'Ambassador Package' for the Polynesian Cultural Center — it includes priority access, reserved luau seating, and a personal guide. Book tickets well in advance for summer visits. The center is open Monday–Saturday; plan accordingly. This is an extraordinary cultural and entertainment experience for the entire family.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Windward Coast of Oahu — drive the scenic Pali Highway through the Ko'olau Mountains and visit the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for dramatic panoramic views. Continue to Kailua Beach, consistently ranked among the best beaches in America, for a morning of swimming, paddleboarding, and kayaking in crystal-clear turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayak to the Mokulua Islands (Na Mokulua) — two small offshore islets accessible by kayak from Kailua Beach. Explore hidden coves, pristine beaches, and nesting seabirds. Rent premium kayaks through a local outfitter or arrange a guided kayak tour.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the charming Kailua town, followed by a scenic drive back to East Oahu along the coast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or stop at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for its red velvet pancakes and island-style breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the Mokulua Islands — arrange a gourmet picnic basket through the hotel concierge with premium sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse (Kailua) — a beloved local institution serving premium steaks and fresh seafood in a relaxed tropical setting

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach parking can be limited on weekends — arrive early or arrange a drop-off. Kayak rentals and guided tours to the Mokulua Islands are available through Kailua Beach Adventures. Life jackets are required and provided. The kayak crossing is approximately 0.5 miles each way — suitable for older children and adults. Younger children can ride in tandem kayaks with parents.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — experience the island from above with a luxury helicopter flight covering the Ko'olau Mountains, Sacred Falls, Chinaman's Hat, the North Shore, and dramatic coastal cliffs. Many tours offer doors-off options for photographers. A truly unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a profoundly moving and historically significant experience. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pacific Aviation Museum. Arrange a premium guided tour for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Final celebration dinner at one of Honolulu's most prestigious restaurants. Reflect on the incredible week of experiences over a world-class meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final leisurely morning meal before a busy day
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center café or nearby — keep it simple and efficient to maximize time at the memorial
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel (Waikiki) — Honolulu's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurant, offering French-inspired cuisine with Hawaiian ingredients in an elegant oceanfront setting; perfect for a special farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Private helicopter tours should be booked well in advance through operators like Blue Hawaiian Helicopters or Paradise Helicopters. Pearl Harbor requires free timed-entry passes for the USS Arizona Memorial — reserve online in advance as they fill up quickly. The full Pearl Harbor experience takes 3–4 hours. La Mer at Halekulani requires formal attire and advance reservations — book as early as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a slow, luxurious breakfast at the hotel. Take one last walk along Hanauma Bay's shoreline to soak in the views. Pack, check out, and collect any final souvenirs or local products (Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt, local artwork).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional final activity such as a relaxing beachside massage on the sand, a visit to the Honolulu Museum of Art, or last-minute shopping at the Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air shopping mall in the US) featuring luxury brands and local boutiques. Private luxury transfer to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu. Access the premier airport lounge for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Final grand hotel breakfast — go all out with the full menu, fresh tropical juices, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Ala Moana Center — Mariposa at Neiman Marcus offers a beautiful, upscale dining experience with views of Ala Moana Beach Park
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11:00 AM — request a late check-out (1:00–2:00 PM) through the concierge if your flight departs in the evening. Arrange private luxury airport transfer in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases home to avoid baggage complications. Mahalo for a wonderful trip — Hawaii will be waiting for your return!
